title: THE ULTIMATE DO EVERYTHING BIKE? THE ARGON 18 KRYPTON PRO: AN IN DEPTH REVIEW

takeaways.text: He repeats tire limits of about 40 mm with 1×, about 35 mm with a Shimano 2× road groupset and about 38 mm with SRAM 2×, depending on tire and rim; his own bike runs 32 mm Schwalbe Pro One tires on 25 mm-internal rims.
A down-tube storage compartment holds a supplied tool roll behind a lever-released cover under the bottle cage.
The Krypton Pro is sold as a frameset (about 900 g claimed) with one SRAM Red build; the non-Pro Krypton shares geometry and features but uses a heavier layup and comes in several builds.
On early rides in Spain it climbed better than he expected for an endurance bike and descended calmly without twitchiness.

The 3D+ headset system offers flush, 15 mm and 30 mm top-cap extensions (claimed 5% and 11% stiffer than spacers); routing enters at the headset while stem, bars and a round 27.2 mm seatpost stay standard.
T47 threaded bottom bracket and many mounts for fenders, racks, extra bottles and a top-tube bag; a non-Pro Krypton with Rival, Hunt wheels and Vittoria tires was quoted at 8.62 kg.

disclosure: The presenter states he is sponsored by Argon 18, Shimano, Schwalbe and ENVE, whose products are on the bike.
summary: A sponsored rider's in-depth first review of the second-generation Krypton Pro frameset built with Dura-Ace 9200 and ENVE wheels, with notes on the non-Pro Krypton.
